precepts.text: For our conversation is in heaven, from whence also we look for the Saviour, the Lord Jesus Christ. We can't be entangled with the affairs of this life. What does God want us to do? What does God require of us? What is God's mission? Gather the twelve tribes of Israel from the four corners of the earth. Let the elect be sealed; let the 144 be sealed, so we can go home.
precepts.point: That he may please him who hath chosen him to be a soldier: in order for us to please God, who have called us to be a soldier, we cannot be entangled with the affairs of this life. If you entangled with the affairs of this life, that means you want to please men. We can't move like that. We got to be good soldiers with the mind of a judge, which comes from that biblical education.

note.label: Perilous Times: Judges and Soldiers

precepts.why:
If Christ is our commander, what does that make us? Soldiers. “Thou therefore endure hardness, as a good soldier of Jesus Christ.” And a soldier cannot live for this world: “For our conversation is in heaven; from whence also we look for the Saviour, the Lord Jesus Christ.”

We are at war. Spiritual war. We don’t use guns or weapons or any of that stuff, but we are at spiritual war, and spiritual war is the most powerful mode of warfare. Our forefathers understood that in this gospel, this mission we are on, we are all soldiers on the battlefield. That is how Paul referred to his fellow laborers.

“No man that warreth entangleth himself with the affairs of this life; that he may please him who hath chosen him to be a soldier.” In order to please God, who has called us to be soldiers, we cannot be entangled with the affairs of this life. If you are entangled with the affairs of this life, that means you want to please men. We can’t move like that. Our conversation is in heaven, and we are looking for the Saviour to come from there.

So what does God want us to do? What does God require of us? What is God’s mission? Gather the twelve tribes of Israel from the four corners of the earth. Let the elect be sealed; let the 144 be sealed, so we can go home. That is the business of a good soldier of Jesus Christ, with the mind of a judge that comes from biblical education, instead of the affairs of this life.

precepts.text: Whose end is destruction, whose God is their belly, and whose glory is in their shame, who mind earthly things. That is what minding earthly things means, and that is how it is with many Israelite camps today: everything becomes about the flesh instead of the godly things of the Lord.
precepts.point: Mortify therefore your members which are upon the earth: mortify means to deaden. Fornication, uncleanness, inordinate affection, evil concupiscence: sexual sins. And covetousness, which is idolatry: because when your god is your own flesh and you want to please that and only that, it is idolatry.

note.label: Deceived by Enticing Words: Colossians 2

precepts.why:
“Set your affection on things above, not on things on the earth.” Is Paul saying don’t get a job, don’t become an entrepreneur, don’t get married? No. He is talking about sexuality. The thought continues from the end of Colossians 2:23: “not in any honour to the satisfying of the flesh.”

Philippians shows what minding the things on the earth looks like: “Whose end is destruction, whose God is their belly, and whose glory is in their shame, who mind earthly things.” When the flesh is your focus, your aim and your goal, you are minding earthly things.

That is how it is with many Israelite camps today: to hell with the godly things of the Lord, I want sex, sex and more sex, give it to me now. Men in those camps talk of two, three, four wives, and it becomes sexual immorality all over the place; those wicked spirits are back today. That is why Paul says to mortify the members upon the earth, “fornication, uncleanness, inordinate affection, evil concupiscence, and covetousness, which is idolatry”: when your god is your own flesh and you want to please that and only that, it is idolatry.

precepts.text: The holy spirit of discipline will flee deceit, and remove from thoughts that are without understanding. Discipline is a holy spirit with a cap and a limit; the man who cannot stop eating worships himself. You cannot obtain discipline without the Holy Spirit, and there are levels to it, up to the disciples working miracles. Full access comes through disciplining the food intake and the sex outtake, the two stumbling blocks that keep us from progressing.
precepts.point: Whose glory is in their shame, who mind earthly things: when am I going to eat, the things pleasing to the eyes and the flesh. Overindulging outside God's guidelines takes you out of the realm of discipline into the realm of Satan.

note.label: Power Under Control: Food, Sex & Self-Mastery

precepts.why:
Paul speaks of those “Whose end is destruction, whose God is their belly, and whose glory is in their shame, who mind earthly things.” When we overindulge excessively, outside the guidelines God gave us, we start to operate outside the realm of God, outside the realm of discipline, and into the realm of Satan. That is why God gave us a law.

“For the holy spirit of discipline will flee deceit, and remove from thoughts that are without understanding.” The Bible says discipline is a holy spirit. There is a cap and a limit. The man who cannot stop eating is worshipping himself, because God says to eat in moderation and to eat what nourishes; do not eat just to eat. Christ said his meat was to do the will of the Father, but people followed him just for the food, because their god was the belly.

Discipline has to be practiced. People wonder why they cannot obtain discipline: it is because they do not have the Holy Spirit. There is a level of the Holy Spirit given to you because you know your nationality, but there are levels to accessing it and gaining power in it. The disciples reached the level where they worked miracles.

Full access to the Holy Spirit comes through disciplining our food intake and our sex outtake. Food and sex are closely related in the body: one is for procreation of life, the other for nourishing that life. Those two are our stumbling blocks, the two things that keep us from progressing and moving forward.

precepts.text: Be not excessive toward any, and without discretion do nothing. Ask why you are eating: nourishment, or because it looks, smells, tastes, and sounds good five minutes after you ate? A nymphomaniac wants sex all the time, but sex was created for procreation and beyond that becomes pleasure, and there is no level of pleasure at which the flesh is finally fulfilled. What high are you looking for when you smoke weed, since you always come down? There is only fulfillment in disciplining your spirit and keeping the commandments.
precepts.point: Whose glory is in their shame, who mind earthly things: when am I going to eat, the things pleasing to the eyes and the flesh. Overindulging outside God's guidelines takes you out of the realm of discipline into the realm of Satan.

note.label: Power Under Control: Food, Sex & Self-Mastery

precepts.why:
“Be not excessive toward any; and without discretion do nothing.” Do not be excessive toward anything. You might say, but I am hungry. Then ask yourself why you are eating. Is it for nourishment, the proper nutrients? Or because it looks good, smells good, tastes good, because you like the sound of it? Are outside things programming you, catering to the lust of the flesh through your eyes and your ears? Did you eat just five minutes ago and now you have to get a snack?

Some are excessive even with sex, a nymphomaniac, wanting sex all the time. Sex was created for procreation; outside of that it becomes pleasure. How much pleasure until the body is completely fulfilled? There is never an end to it. The same with weed: what high are you looking for, when you always come down? There is no fulfillment in smoking weed, drinking alcohol, the excess of sex, or overeating.

That is why the scriptures speak of the holy spirit of discipline. The only fulfillment is in disciplining your spirit and keeping God’s commandments. Once you go outside the realm of discipline, you are catering to the realm of Satan, and you open yourself to be a target and to be controlled at any level. That is the mind of those who “mind earthly things” in Philippians 3.

precepts.text: They that are such serve not our Lord Jesus Christ, but their own belly. Biggie said he only sold crack to feed his family; his stomach became his god. Your vessel is an indicator of who you serve: your look, conduct, speech, and character tell who your god is. If you are grotesquely overweight, outside a natural diet, you are your own god, the same self-worship as a birthday. The good news is you can control it.
precepts.point: Whose glory is in their shame, who mind earthly things: when am I going to eat, the things pleasing to the eyes and the flesh. Overindulging outside God's guidelines takes you out of the realm of discipline into the realm of Satan.

note.label: Power Under Control: Food, Sex & Self-Mastery

precepts.why:
“For they that are such serve not our Lord Jesus Christ, but their own belly.” This is the same people Paul wept over in Philippians 3, “whose God is their belly”: the wicked of our people. The scribes and Pharisees could not resist the wisdom of Christ or deny his miracles, but they loved the position Rome placed them in, the accolades, the greetings in the marketplace, and what comes with authority: food and sex. They crept into women’s houses as in Susanna; Eli’s sons exploited the women at the temple, because position and status bring money, power and respect.

They serve their own fleshly pleasures and lusts: let me get over on this person, let me defraud him, let me steal, so I can fill my own belly. Biggie said he was only selling crack to feed his family. He did not serve the Lord Jesus Christ; his own stomach became his god.

Your vessel is an indicator of who you serve. By the way you look, carry yourself, your conduct, your speech and your character, we can tell who your master is. People are going to get mad, but if you are grotesquely overweight, outside the realm of a natural diet, then you are your own god. You say you do not celebrate birthdays, the highest satanic celebration of oneself, yet if you cannot control your food intake, your god is your belly, and that is you.

The good thing is you can control it and do something about it, just like you control whether you celebrate birthdays. God looks at things differently than we do, so we have to reframe our mindset into the mind of Christ and the Father.

precepts.text: Paul lays out his resume: circumcised the eighth day, of the stock of Israel, the tribe of Benjamin, a Hebrew of the Hebrews, a Pharisee; concerning zeal, persecuting the church; touching the righteousness of the law, blameless.
precepts.point: Therefore they that were scattered abroad went every where preaching the word. Because of the great persecution the disciples had to flee, and our fathers were fugitives, always on the run, the way it was done to men like Nat Turner. It is going to come to that point again, where a brother might have to house a teacher whose name is on the news, wanted for sedition; you might be charged as guilty by association, but you have to see past it to protect your brother, because the gospel has to go forward. This is why we need such a high level of unity and love for one another to survive.

note.label: Acts 8: The Word Scattered Abroad, and the Baptism unto the Conscience

precepts.why:
Paul lays out his resume: “Circumcised the eighth day, of the stock of Israel, of the tribe of Benjamin, an Hebrew of the Hebrews; as touching the law, a Pharisee; Concerning zeal, persecuting the church; touching the righteousness which is in the law, blameless.”

An Israelite of the tribe of Benjamin, a Pharisee, blameless touching the righteousness of the law, and his zeal went into persecuting the church. That is who was driving the disciples out to be scattered abroad, and it is why they went everywhere preaching the word.

precepts.text: Circumcised the eighth day, of the stock of Israel, the tribe of Benjamin, a Hebrew of the Hebrews, a Pharisee, and touching the righteousness in the law blameless.
precepts.point: Saul spends certain days with the disciples at Damascus and straightway preaches Christ in the synagogues, that he is the Son of God. Paul constantly has to give his resume, because he came up under Christ, not under the apostles, so the churches needed to know where he came from.

note.label: Acts 9: A Chosen Vessel

precepts.why:
Paul constantly has to give his resume, because he came up under Christ, not under the apostles, so the churches needed to know where he came from. “Circumcised the eighth day, of the stock of Israel, of the tribe of Benjamin, an Hebrew of the Hebrews; as touching the law, a Pharisee; Concerning zeal, persecuting the church; touching the righteousness which is in the law, blameless.”

Circumcised the eighth day, of the stock of Israel, the tribe of Benjamin, a Hebrew of the Hebrews, a Pharisee, and touching the righteousness in the law blameless. This is the man who, straightway after certain days with the disciples at Damascus, preached Christ in the synagogues, that he is the Son of God.

precepts.text: Paul was circumcised the eighth day, of the tribe of Benjamin, a Pharisee, because the Pharisees upheld circumcision.
precepts.point: So the circumcision was primarily the southern kingdom, Judah, raised in the law, and the Pharisees who pushed circumcision above everything, even above faith and the commandments; the uncircumcision was the northern kingdom and the scattered Israelites.

note.label: Acts 11: The Gentiles Are Scattered Israel

precepts.why:
Paul was “Circumcised the eighth day, of the stock of Israel, of the tribe of Benjamin, an Hebrew of the Hebrews; as touching the law, a Pharisee.”

Paul was of the southern kingdom, Benjamin, and a Pharisee, and the Pharisees upheld circumcision. That is the party of the circumcision that contended with Peter.

precepts.point: He called himself the chief of sinners. 2 Corinthians 12:7 says a thorn in the flesh was given to him, the messenger of Satan, lest he be exalted above measure.

note.label: Galatians 1: Paul's Apostleship and the True Gospel

precepts.why:
Paul “profited in the Jews’ religion above many my equals in mine own nation”, and Philippians gives his credentials: “If any other man thinketh that he hath whereof he might trust in the flesh, I more: Circumcised the eighth day, of the stock of Israel, of the tribe of Benjamin, an Hebrew of the Hebrews; as touching the law, a Pharisee; Concerning zeal, persecuting the church; touching the righteousness which is in the law, blameless.”

Paul was a Pharisee, a separated one, of the Pharisaical order, and he was the top of his class. His conversation in times past under the law was as a Pharisee, and his zeal was “persecuting the church”, which is what he means when he says “beyond measure I persecuted the church of God, and wasted it.” Yet “what things were gain to me, those I counted loss for Christ.”
